doc.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Ray Conniff and the choral piano records at Capitol
summary: A choral record leads to how Capitol wanted piano with a choral group.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I have another selection here that goes back a ways. It’s really a different style. I’m curious about why this particular kind of music was being done at the time. I think you’ll probably recognize this.

Yeah well that’s Ray Conniff who was in Bunny Berigan’s band, we were together, and he did some choral records for Columbia, for Mitch Miller, and they seemed to catch on and Capitol wanted me to use a choral group with the piano. That’s how that came about.
And this was around what year? Do you remember? I have the record here.
Yeah. There seemed to be a whole kind of, a lot of instrumental music popular even into the 50’s.
